title: Energy in a more dangerous world | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Energy Gang live episode at Climate Week NYC frames resilience, affordability and self-sufficiency as the new energy priorities, arguing that the combination of a new era of conflict and AI breakthroughs creates genuinely new challenges for a more complex, harder-to-afford energy system.

insights.so_what: Cheap asymmetric weapons raise physical-risk premia on concentrated energy infrastructure.

insights.claim: Middle East conflict, drone attacks on critical infrastructure and threats to international shipping are forcing a rethink of how to build shock-absorbing energy systems without raising consumer costs.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Shipping and infrastructure threats feed into energy-security capex and freight risk.

insights.claim: Climate policy becomes much harder to sustain when voters no longer feel they can afford the transition, even though climate risks have not gone away.
